title: Liveness, readiness, and startup probes that tell the orchestrator the truth, at the resolved paths
asA: platform operator running the service under Kubernetes
iWant: three probe endpoints (at their resolved paths) that each answer their one question honestly and cheaply
soThat: the orchestrator restarts, routes, and rolls out instances on real signals

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET on the resolved liveness path returns 200 with the specified response schema whenever the process can serve any request, and performs no dependency checks whatsoever.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running instance with a deliberately unreachable database and the liveness path resolved either by observability-probe-endpoints (Kubernetes profile default /live) or by project configuration
acceptanceCriteria.when: the resolved liveness path is called
acceptanceCriteria.then: it returns 200 against the specified schema, unaffected by the dependency outage

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET on the resolved readiness path returns 200 only when every declared downstream dependency check (database, cache, queues) passes.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an instance with all declared dependencies reachable and the readiness path resolved (Kubernetes profile default /ready) or supplied by project configuration
acceptanceCriteria.when: the resolved readiness path is called
acceptanceCriteria.then: it returns 200 with the specified schema listing each check as passing

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET on the resolved readiness path returns 503 with a body enumerating the failed checks by name when any declared dependency is unreachable.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an instance with one declared dependency down and the readiness path resolved as above
acceptanceCriteria.when: the resolved readiness path is called
acceptanceCriteria.then: it returns 503 and the body names the failing check while still listing the passing ones

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET on the resolved startup path returns 200 only after initialisation (migrations applied, cache warmed, config loaded) completes, and a non-200 with the pending steps before that. The startup path is available when the composed observability-probe-endpoints blueprint enables it via `probeInterface.options.kubernetes.startup.enabled: true` or the project supplies `probeInterface.paths.startup` in configuration.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an instance mid-initialisation and the same instance after initialisation, with the startup path resolved (Kubernetes profile default /startup when enabled) or supplied by project configuration
acceptanceCriteria.when: the resolved startup path is called in each state
acceptanceCriteria.then: the mid-initialisation call is non-200 naming pending steps; the post-initialisation call is 200

acceptanceCriteria.description: All three probes sit outside the auth middleware and outside rate limiting: the auth-middleware installer consumes exactly the resolved probe path set (the same list observability-probe-endpoints emits via TAC-1501 getExemptPathSet, or the exact set derived from `probeInterface.paths` in the essentials-alone case), so each probe succeeds with no credentials and is never 401, 403, or 429; adjacent routes never fall under the same exemption.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running instance with the resolved probe path set exposed to the auth-middleware installer
acceptanceCriteria.when: each probe is called with no credentials at sustained frequency AND an adjacent user-traffic route is also called unauthenticated
acceptanceCriteria.then: every probe call is answered on probe semantics alone, never with an auth or rate-limit status; the adjacent route returns the auth middleware unauthenticated response

acceptanceCriteria.description: Probe requests (at their resolved paths) do not appear in info-level request logs and are excluded from RED endpoint metrics; probe outcomes are recorded under their own dedicated metric.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a period of steady probe traffic on the resolved probe paths
acceptanceCriteria.when: info-level logs and endpoint metrics are inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: probe requests appear in neither, and the dedicated probe-outcome metric carries their results

acceptanceCriteria.description: The generated OpenAPI document names the three probe surfaces (liveness, readiness, startup) and their resolved paths, plus each probes success and failure schemas and its documented failure mode; the resolved paths are computed at documentation-generation time from the composed observability-probe-endpoints blueprint or from project configuration.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the generated OpenAPI document produced for a project that has resolved its probe paths
acceptanceCriteria.when: the three probe entries are read
acceptanceCriteria.then: each declares its success and failure schemas and its documented failure mode; every entry path is the resolved path (no legacy literal probe-path prefix appears in the generated document)

acceptanceCriteria.description: Readiness reflects recovery: when a failed dependency becomes reachable again, GET on the resolved readiness path returns to 200 without a process restart.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an instance whose dependency outage has been restored
acceptanceCriteria.when: the resolved readiness path is called after restoration
acceptanceCriteria.then: it returns 200 without the process having restarted
